title: Mini-Onboard ProbeKit playbook and telemetry notes
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a small, portable onboarding playbook ("ProbeKit") for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs for the first time. Goal: get a developer from zero to an instrumented sample app in ~30–60 minutes with clear telemetry and smoke tests so we can (a) verify runtime assumptions, (b) collect baseline perf/cost metrics, and (c) provide a reproducible pattern for future docs/labs.

What this doc is: rough, opinionated, intentionally minimal. Not a full curriculum. Think: pocket lab + checklist + telemetry contract.

Core principles
- Minimal friction: CLI + single Python sample + single Node snippet.
- Telemetry-first: require 6 baseline signals before we call an onramp "complete".
- Failure clarity: show both graceful fallback and debug path.
- Reproducible: deterministic sample prompts + seedable randomness.

Quick flow (30–60m)
1) Create API key + set env var (5m)
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxxx
2) Run sample app in local dev (10m)
   - python run_sample.py or node run_sample.js
3) Trigger three scenarios (10–15m)
   - normal short text gen, long context gen ( > 2k tokens), embeddings batch (10 items)
4) Check telemetry dashboard + smoke logs (5–10m)
   - validate p50/p95, error_rate, token_cost per request
5) Do one canary failure (10m)
   - simulate transient network or model OOM, observe fallback to smaller model or cached response

Sample acceptance checklist (what we consider "onboarded")
- Sample app runs locally and completes all three scenarios without code edits.
- Telemetry shows: latency_p50, latency_p95, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, error_count.
- Smoke tests pass: health-check endpoint returns 200; fallback route returns cached payload when upstream fails.
- Developer can reproduce a perf run and capture a small CSV of metrics.

Baseline telemetry contract (required signals)
- request_id: uuid string
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- model: string (e.g., redwood/gpt-small-quantized)
- model_variant: string (fallback/primary)
- seq_len_in: integer (approx prompt tokens)
- seq_len_out: integer (generated tokens)
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end)
- status: success | failure | fallback
- error_code: string (nullable)
- cost_usd_estimate: float (optional but preferred)

Event examples (log lines)
- INFO telemetry event: {request_id, model, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, latency_ms, status}
- ERROR telemetry event: {request_id, error_code, stack_snippet}

Developer ritual (mini runbook)
- Step 0: open terminal, create venv, export REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Step 1: run local sample; keep console open
- Step 2: run smoke tests ./smoke/run_all.sh (or npm test)
- Step 3: open telemetry URL (local dev: http://localhost:8080/telemetry)
- Step 4: if latency_p95 > SLO, toggle batching=off, rerun scenario to reproduce
- Step 5: file brief note in Jira (JIRA-ENG-xxxx) with sample_id and CSV snapshot

Sample CLI + Python snippet (intentionally tiny)
- Shell: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-small","prompt":"Write a 3-line haiku about shipping","max_tokens":60}'

- Python (requests)
  import os
  import requests
  api_key = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}'}, json={'model': 'redwood/gpt-small', 'prompt': 'haiku about shipping', 'max_tokens': 60})
  print(r.json())

Key smoke tests (commands)
- health-check: curl localhost:9000/health -> 200
- sample-gen: python run_sample.py --prompt "short" -> exit 0 + JSON output length > 0
- fallback: toggle env REDWOOD_FORCE_FAIL=true, run sample -> status == fallback

Scenario matrix (what to test in the kit)
- Latency-sensitive: short prompts, streaming=true, small model, expect p50<100ms local dev
- Throughput: 10 concurrent requests, join batching path, measure tokens/sec
- Cost: embeddings 10x batch vs 10 single – compare token cost per item
- Resilience: simulate zone outage -> automatic fallback model variant

Observability tasks for eng-devexp (what we should implement in ProbeKit)
- Lightweight local telemetry collector binary (writes JSONL to ./telemetry/output.jsonl)
- Small dashboard template (Grafana/Tempo) with p50/p95, errors, cost estimate aggregated by model
- Smoke runner to exercise scenarios and emit telemetry in canonical schema

Developer-facing docs surface (short list)
- Quickstart: zero-to-sample (single-page) + copyable commands
- Telemetry contract: one pager with example payloads
- Debug guide: common failure codes and where to find logs
- FAQ: keys, rate limits, debugging timeouts

Unresolved / to discuss
- Cost_estimate: do we compute internally or accept SDK reported estimate? (ask infra-team)
- Default SLO values for local dev vs dedicated: should we ship recommendations?
- Should the ProbeKit include an embeddable dashboard or just a link to a template?

Implementation notes / quick engineering TODOs
- probekit/service: add endpoint /probe/metrics that returns last N telemetry events (quick grep)
- smoke/runner: make deterministic: set seed, fixed prompts, synthetic user IDs
- telemetry: include small sampling header to avoid high volume in CI
- docs: add one-line diff with existing quickstarts to avoid duplication (see linked PR)

Notes to self (style + empathy)
- Keep first pass frictionless: one command to get telem + CSV. If devs need to open multiple UIs they drop off.
- Make the sample app feel like a real tiny app (chat UI + logs) so teams copy the pattern.
- Avoid heavy infra: no K8s required for first pass. Local-only + optional cloud mode.

Quick references
- Github PR with sample: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probekit/pull/7
- Existing onboarding collateral: CONFLUENCE-ONBOARD-824
- Related Jira: JIRA-ENG-4821 (probekit epic)

Last-minute checklist before handing to docs/ux
- [ ] finalize telemetry field names (consistency with console)
- [ ] add copyable curl & python + node snippets
- [ ] short smoke script that exits 0 on success
- [ ] 1-page quickstart PDF for sales demos

End of notes — keep iterating. This is deliberately terse; will expand to a full lab with artifacts once we validate the minimal flow with 3 internal teams.

-- Asha
